1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with clear heading hierarchy and comfortable line spacing, though spacing is standard rather than notably generous.

2.why: No italics or dense paragraphs appear, but the step indicator 'STEP 1 OF 5' and 'MFA' are set in all-caps, so the claim only partly holds.

3.why: The single-column layout fits the mobile viewport with legible text sizes, clear labels, and a full-width button.

4.why: Instructions are short and plain ('Confirm your bank account details to protect higher-value payments'), though the unexplained acronym 'MFA' adds slight jargon.

5.why: Both fields show example values ('marcus@example.test', '+15551234567') and a hint explicitly says 'use the displayed example details.'

6.why: Every screen contains only short lines of text; no long block of text is required to proceed.

7.why: No long codes or secrets are ever displayed (the flow never advances past sign-in), so no copy affordance is observed.

8.why: No QR code or manual-entry alternative appears anywhere; even the screenshot labelled 'authenticator setup' only shows the sign-in error page.

9.why: Standard text inputs are shown but there is no password field and no observable evidence of autofill or password-manager support.

10.why: A 'STEP 1 OF 5' indicator and a single prominent blue 'Continue securely' button make the step and primary action unmistakable.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one primary action (the 'Continue securely' button) with no competing calls to action.

12.why: After submission the banner 'Unable to sign in with those details' states the failure but gives no indication of what happens or what to do next.

13.why: Screenshots 2–4 show repeated attempts with field values retained and no lockout or penalty, though no reveal/hide/re-request-code controls are observed because no codes appear.

14.why: The error message is neutral and non-blaming but does not explain how to fix the problem, only that sign-in failed.

15.why: No countdown, timeout, or time limit is visible on any screen, though code entry is never reached so entry-time generosity cannot be directly confirmed.
